numeral.purpose: Numpad digits and large status numbers (visit counts, days-until-expiry). Must read from arm's length.

shadows.name: key-rest
shadows.purpose: Numpad key at rest — hard, mechanical shadow.

shadows.name: key-pressed
shadows.purpose: Numpad key mid-press, paired with translateY(2px).

shadows.name: card-elevation
shadows.purpose: Confirmation card and overlays — soft, ambient, floating.

motion.name: card-entrance

components.name: Numpad Key
components.description: A single digit key on the check-in numpad — the signature component.
components.css: .ds-numpad-key { width: 72px; height: 72px; background: #FFFFFF; color: #15181C; border: 1px solid #C7CDD3; border-radius: 6px; font-family: 'Archivo Black', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 40px; font-weight: 800; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 #C7CDD3; transition: transform 80ms ease-out, box-shadow 80ms ease-out; } .ds-numpad-key:active { transform: translateY(2px); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 #C7CDD3; } .ds-numpad-key:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3A4046; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Check-In Confirm Key
components.description: Full-width primary action key; disabled until a valid number is entered.
components.css: .ds-confirm-key { width: 100%; height: 72px; background: #F2B705; color: #15181C; border: none; border-radius: 6px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.02em; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 #C9990A; transition: transform 80ms ease-out, box-shadow 80ms ease-out; } .ds-confirm-key:active { transform: translateY(2px); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 #C9990A; } .ds-confirm-key:disabled { background: #C7CDD3; color: #5A6167; box-shadow: none; } .ds-confirm-key:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3A4046; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Status Badge Active
components.description: Active membership status, always paired with the text label.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 6px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-badge-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-badge-active { background: rgba(63, 143, 95, 0.12); color: #3F8F5F; } .ds-badge-active .ds-badge-dot { background: #3F8F5F; }

components.name: Confirmation Card
components.description: Centered overlay shown on successful check-in; auto-dismisses after 2.5s.

components.name: Tab Bar Item
components.description: One of four persistent bottom-tab destinations.
components.css: .ds-tab-item { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 64px; background: #F1F2F0; border: none; color: #3A4046; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; } .ds-tab-item-active { color: #15181C; font-weight: 600; border-top: 2px solid #F2B705; }

narrative.overview: RackIn's one screen-job is getting a staff member from "who just walked in" to "checked in, confirmed" in under two seconds, standing up, often one-handed, under variable light, repeated every twenty seconds at peak. That job is the brief — this is a tool that lives on a counter, closer in spirit to a point-of-sale terminal, a shop scale, or gym equipment itself than to a SaaS product or admin dashboard. The numpad is the signature element and the brand: every other screen stays quiet and functional so the numpad can read as a physical control — chunky, high-contrast, satisfying to press, styled after gym equipment keypads and weight-plate numerals rather than a generic phone dialer. The palette pulls from gym hardware itself: brushed steel, rubber flooring, chalk dust, and the one warning-tape yellow found on a loading bay.
keyCharacteristics: The numpad is treated as a physical control, not a form input.
Near-neutral steel/chalk base keeps the interface calm and legible under variable front-desk lighting.
Color carries meaning only — yellow means press this, red/green mean expired/active — never decoration.
Flat, solid, pressable surfaces; no glassy neumorphism.
Minimal, purposeful motion only; nothing decorative or scroll-triggered.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Color Rule
rules.body: Yellow, red, and green never decorate. Yellow means press this, green means active/paid, red means expired/lapsed — nothing else on screen carries color.

rules.name: The Arm's-Length Rule
rules.body: Numerals a staff member must read at a glance while standing never drop below the Numeral role's weight and size.

rules.name: The One-Tap-Away Rule
rules.body: Every core destination stays reachable in exactly one tap, always visible, no menu to open first.

rules.name: The Mechanical-Not-Ambient Rule
rules.body: Shadows on interactive controls are hard-edged and state-driven. Shadows on passive containers may be soft and ambient. Don't mix the two vocabularies on the same element.

dos: Do treat the numpad as a physical control, not a form: real press depth, a distinct confirm key.
Do reserve yellow, red, and green strictly for their assigned meanings.
Do pair every status color with a text label.
Do keep every touch target at least 56px (72px for numpad keys).
donts: Don't use warm cream + terracotta serif, near-black + neon accent, or broadsheet hairline-newspaper styling.
Don't add a hamburger menu, nested navigation, or hide any of the four core destinations behind a menu.
Don't add decorative motion (parallax, page-load choreography, scroll-triggered reveals).
